Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Only 11 participants contribute 200 imbalanced conversations, with self-reported demographic/diagnostic data and cultural/language restriction. Pooled tests treat conversations as independent despite repeated participants. The authors explicitly exclude clinical mental-health validation and safety-critical deployment decisions from the benchmark’s intended use.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Eleven US native-English adult participants produce 200 conversations with eight anonymized original models. Diagnostic data are self-reported; conversations are not independent participants.
  • GPT-4o-mini suggests question subsets that participants may revise. Golden responses are participant-edited after viewing original and preference-informed model outputs, rather than independent wholly human-written references.
  • Eleven evaluation models predict participant annotations. Default does not use future turns; Omniscient includes privileged profiles. Mistral Large draft scores and Kendall tau are supplementary and excluded from the Composite.
  • Pooled tests assume conversation independence despite repeated participants. Conversation-level Pearson r=-0.097 and model-level Spearman rho=-0.36 have different statistical units and are not interchangeable.
  • The human baseline has three raters and seven conversations. Small imbalanced culturally restricted samples and self-report limit interpretation; the authors explicitly exclude clinical validation and safety-critical deployment use.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AttuneBench uses 200 multi-turn human/model conversations from 11 US native English participants. Participants supply emotional-state, observed/preferred behavior and response-ranking annotations, with GPT-4o-mini suggesting question subsets and a preference-informed model response helping the reference-editing workflow. Default evaluation predicts annotations without future turns; draft-judge scores are supplementary, not Composite inputs.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Within the default-mode eleven-model panel, Emotion F1 did not reach omnibus significance(p=0.099), while Pairwise Accuracy differentiated model behavior more strongly. The paper’s conversation-level correlations and model-level correlations are separately defined; these findings do not validate a universal one-dimensional emotional-intelligence ranking.
